seoTitle: How to Fix Outlook/Hotmail 'Too Many Requests' Error 429
metaDescription: Fix the Hotmail or Outlook 'Too Many Requests' error 429 caused by frequent logins or refreshes with these step-by-step solutions.
intro: The Outlook or Hotmail 'Too Many Requests' error 429 usually shows up when Microsoft temporarily limits your account activity due to frequent logins, refreshes, or suspicious behavior flags. This guide walks through why this error happens and the steps to resolve it.

steps.heading: Wait out the temporary lock
steps.body: In many cases, this error clears on its own after a short waiting period as Microsoft's rate limit resets.

steps.heading: Clear browser cache and cookies
steps.body: Clear cached data for Outlook or Hotmail in your browser, then try accessing your account again.

steps.heading: Reset your internet connection
steps.body: Restart your router or switch networks, since repeated requests from the same connection can sometimes trigger this limit.

steps.heading: Try a different device or browser
steps.body: Log in from another device or browser to check whether the issue is tied to your original session.

steps.heading: Avoid rapid refreshing or repeated logins
steps.body: Going forward, avoid refreshing or logging in repeatedly in a short time span, since this is a common trigger for the error.

faq.question: How long does the 429 error usually last?
faq.answer: It's typically temporary and can clear within minutes to a few hours, depending on how the rate limit was triggered.

faq.question: Does this error mean my account was hacked?
faq.answer: Not necessarily — it's more often related to activity patterns like frequent refreshes rather than a security breach.

faq.question: Can using multiple devices at once cause this error?
faq.answer: Yes, logging in and refreshing from several devices simultaneously can contribute to triggering the rate limit.

faq.question: Will clearing my cache delete my emails?
faq.answer: No, clearing your browser cache doesn't delete emails, which remain stored safely on Microsoft's servers.
